models.name: EnergiPak 3840 portable power station / solar generator, 3840 Wh, 48 V pack of 40135 LiFePO4 cells, 3300 W @ 120 V AC out

gotchas: NO COMMUNICATION OF ANY KIND IS DOCUMENTED, and the manual is thorough enough that the silence is meaningful. Its Product Specifications table lists ten interfaces — AC charging, XT90 input, AC output, two USB-A, two USB-C, car charging — and every one is a POWER port. The contents page has no app, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, or

USB-C PD100W is a charging port with the PD3.0 protocol. PD is a power-delivery negotiation, not a data link a host can read a state of charge from. Do not let the word 'protocol' on the spec sheet promote this device.

The unit has a display showing state of charge and the manual documents a UPS mode, so the information exists inside the box — it just never leaves it. If somebody wants this in Cabin Hub, the only honest route is a clamp or a plug-in energy meter on its AC output, which is a cabin-pzem job, not a BSLBATT driver.
Filed in no-comms.md with the PowerMax charger. Recorded so nobody researches it twice.
